title: Beethoven: genius and deafness
subject: art
description: Ludwig van Beethoven, from Bonn to Vienna, composed his greatest works while becoming deaf and invented the romantic genius.

hero.hook: Deaf, he composes the anthem of joy for all humanity.

blocks.text: **Ludwig van Beethoven** (**1770**-**1827**) is the archetype of the modern genius: wild hair, iron will, fight against destiny. Beyond the myth, his life marks a rupture: the composer is no longer a court servant, but a sovereign creator.
He transforms entertainment music into philosophical language. And he designed his most vast sound architectures, including the Ninth Symphony, in almost total auditory isolation.

sections.title: From Bonn to Vienna: the equal of princes

blocks.text: Born in  in **1770**, Ludwig grew up under a brutal father, **John**, who wanted to make him the new . Nightly rehearsals forge an early technique… and an iron character. [[Bonn]] [[Mozart]]

blocks.caption: Young Beethoven in Bonn: a childhood under pressure.

blocks.text: In **1792**, he moved to , the musical capital. He studied briefly with **Joseph Haydn**. Piano virtuoso, astonishing improviser, he refuses obsequiousness towards patrons: he wants to be the equal of princes. His youthful style, still classic, already announces violent contrasts and larger forms. [[Vienna]]
So neglected in his Viennese youth, his friends sometimes replaced his worn clothes with new ones while he slept, without him noticing.

Between **1798** and **1801**, tinnitus and hearing loss appear. For a star pianist, it's a disaster. In **1802**, in the village of **Heiligenstadt**, he wrote the **Testament of Heiligenstadt**: letter to his brothers, never sent, where he confesses suicidal thoughts... then chooses to live to compose everything he carries within him.

blocks.caption: The Testament of Heiligenstadt: despair that becomes a decision to create.

blocks.text: Starts the . Symphony No. 3, called *Heroic*, is first dedicated to . When he becomes emperor, Beethoven rages and withdraws the dedication. The work revolutionizes the genre with its length and intensity. [[heroic period]] [[Napoleon Bonaparte]]
To better feel the vibrations, he sawed the legs of his pianos so that they rested directly on the floor.

sections.title: The Ninth: the Ode to Joy

blocks.text: In the twilight of his life, Beethoven was almost completely deaf. In **1824**, he completed the **Ninth Symphony**: for the first time, soloists and choir enter a symphony. The finale is based on  by **Friedrich von Schiller**, transformed into a message of fraternity. [[Ode to Joy]]

blocks.caption: The Ninth: the human voice enters the symphony.

blocks.text: At the creation, unable to hear the ovations, he continues to beat time. The contralto **Caroline Unger** makes him turn around to see the crowd standing. The [[Ode to Joy]] later became a European anthem of peace. His last quartets, harsh and modern, would only be understood decades later.
He would sometimes squeeze a wooden rod between his teeth, the other end on the piano: bone conduction made him “hear” the notes.

Beethoven makes the transition from classicism to: subjectivity, passion, excess. The symphony becomes metaphysical drama. and will live in its shadow. It also paves the way for the [[Romanticism]], where the sound is sufficient in itself. At his funeral in **1827**, more than **20, 000** people followed the procession to Vienna.
